name: Edim Zomimin — Punishment Calculation
notes: Specific rules for calculating the punishment of conspiring witnesses, including the division of monetary penalties among witnesses vs. lashes, and the principle that punishment mirrors what they sought to inflict

name: Edim Zomimin — After Verdict (Not After Execution)
hebrew: עדים זוממין — לאחר גמר דין ולא לאחר מיתה
notes: Dispute between Sages and Sadducees: conspiring witnesses are punished after the verdict is finalized but before execution of the condemned, not only after the condemned is killed

name: Edim Zomimin — Group Testimony Invalidation
notes: Rules regarding when one disqualified or conspiring witness voids an entire group's testimony; dispute between Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi regarding monetary vs. capital cases

name: Hazamat Edim (Impeachment of Witnesses)
notes: The procedural mechanism for rendering witnesses as conspiring (zomemim): witnesses must be impeached personally (alibi-style), not merely contradicted in content

name: Galut — Exile for Unintentional Murder
notes: Detailed laws of who is exiled and who is not: downward vs. upward motion, permission to be in location, optional vs. obligatory activity, blind persons, enemies, and categories of people exempt from exile

name: Goel HaDam — Blood Redeemer's Powers and Limits
notes: Specific halakhot of the blood redeemer: within vs. outside the city of refuge boundary, debate whether killing outside boundary is a mitzva, optional, or forbidden

name: Death of High Priest Releasing Exiled Murderer
notes: The law that an unintentional murderer returns from exile upon the death of the High Priest; types of High Priests whose death effects this release; mothers providing sustenance so exiles won't pray for the Kohen Gadol's death

name: Cities of Refuge — Practical Laws of Residence
notes: Practical rules of residence in the city of refuge: paying rent to Levites, returning to prior office upon release, prohibition on leaving for any purpose including testimony, killing in city requires relocation within city

name: Roads to Cities of Refuge (Derakhim l'Arei Miklat)
notes: Obligation to prepare and straighten roads to cities of refuge; court providing two Torah scholars to accompany the fleeing murderer and dissuade the blood redeemer

name: Malkot — Procedure for Flogging
notes: Detailed procedure for administering lashes: position of condemned, composition and size of the strap, distribution of lashes (one-third front, two-thirds back), role of court crier reciting verses, assessment of physical capacity

name: Malkot — Medical Assessment of Capacity (Shuma)
notes: Requirement to assess beforehand how many lashes the condemned can survive; number must be divisible by three; reassessment after flogging begins; exemption if he cannot receive more

name: Malkot Atones for Karet
notes: The principle that one liable to karet who receives lashes is exempted from karet, based on the verse 'your brother shall be debased before your eyes' — he is restored to brotherhood after flogging

name: Malkot for Multiple Simultaneous Violations
hebrew: מלקות על עבירות מרובות בבת אחת
notes: Case of one who performs a single act and violates multiple prohibitions simultaneously, receiving multiple sets of lashes; illustrative case of plowing with multiple concurrent violations

name: Prohibition of Tattooing (Ketovet Ka'aka)
notes: Laws of the prohibition against tattooing: requires both incision in skin and insertion of dye to be liable; debate whether writing God's name is required

name: Prohibition of Bald Spot in Mourning (Korcha)
notes: Prohibition against making a bald spot on one's head in mourning; multiple incisions yield multiple sets of lashes

name: Prohibition of Rounding Head and Beard (Peot)
notes: Detailed laws of the prohibitions against rounding the corners of the head and marring the edges of the beard; number of lashes for each edge; requirement of razor specifically for beard

name: Nazirite Violations and Lashes
notes: Rules for when a nazirite receives multiple sets of lashes: continuous violation vs. repeated violations after forewarning for wine drinking, corpse impurity, and shaving

name: Shatnez — Lashes for Wearing Mixed Species
notes: The specific rule that wearing shatnez repeatedly after forewarning incurs separate sets of lashes each time; continuous wearing incurs only one set

name: Istatit — Concern of Organized Witness Conspiracy
notes: Rabbi Yehuda's position that when one set of witnesses renders many successive sets conspiring, this raises concern of organized conspiracy (istatit), and only the first set is executed

name: Sanhedrin Charutzit — Destructive vs. Virtuous Tribunal
notes: Dispute regarding a Sanhedrin that executes frequently: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya (once in 70 years = destructive); Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva (would find technical grounds to avoid all executions); Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's response that this increases murderers

name: Reward for Abstaining from Desired Transgression
hebrew: שכר הפורש מן העבירה שנפשו מחמדת
notes: Principle derived from Rabbi Shimon bar Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi: one who refrains from robbery or forbidden relations, which the soul desires, receives greater reward than one who refrains from blood, which the soul loathes

name: Ribui Mitzvot l'Zakot — Multiplying Commandments to Confer Merit
notes: Rabbi Chananya ben Akashya's statement that God multiplied Torah and mitzvot to increase merit for the Jewish people, based on Isaiah 42:21

name: Conspiring Witness Testimony to Disqualify a Priest (Chalal)
notes: Specific case of conspiring witnesses who testified to render a kohen a chalal; punishment is lashes rather than being rendered a chalal themselves
